sources.lesson: A closed Qwen3-Coder value may quote "<parameter=" (maintainer review: "Use <parameter=name> in the template."); an unclosed middle parameter is the same text, so only evidence outside the text can tell them apart. Whitespace between streamed parallel tool calls is template structure, not content.

mlx2_changes.change: Non-strict tools: an opener inside a closed raw value is text unless it is a well-formed tag naming a declared parameter. Strict tools and tools that declare no parameters still reject any opener; the constrained grammar is unchanged.

OutputParser holds whitespace-only content after a tool call: dropped at the end of the output, and before another call when no text has been shown; otherwise emitted with the next text. Streamed and non-streamed content both follow.

validation: tests/test_output.py (new cases for quoted undeclared tags, declared-name rejection for non-strict, strict and schema-less tools, and whitespace between calls whole and per character, including a tolerant fallback). Real Qwen3.5-9B-4bit tool-call outputs from the mlx-vlm GPU run (nine scenarios) replayed through OutputParser: all parse, identical whole and per character, no stray content.
